observations: Photo 0 shows the interior of a chest freezer; the lining appears intact but shows some wear.
Photo 1 shows the front of the unit with a 'Haier THERMOCOOL' sticker.
Significant rust and metal loss are visible along the entire bottom edge in photo 1.
Photo 2 shows the rear of the unit, including the condenser coils and the power cord.
The technical specification sticker on the back in photo 2 is too blurry to read.
Further corrosion is visible at the bottom rear of the cabinet in photo 2.

risks.risk: The unit may not cool or the compressor may be dead.
risks.proof: Video of the unit powered on showing the internal light and frost formation on the walls.

risks.risk: The severe rust at the base may indicate structural failure or damage to internal lines.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the underside and a video of the unit being moved to check stability.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the technical specification sticker on the back to determine capacity.
Video of the freezer plugged in and running.
Close-up photos of the rusted base to assess the depth of the damage.
response.reason: The item is identified as a Haier Thermocool chest freezer. Due to the extensive visible rust and the lack of proof that it functions, it is priced at its worst case as a non-working unit for scrap.
